audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer level chart disagreed with the content layer on all seven rows: phases[0..6].side all read 'Skill' while win[0..5] read 'Irelia' and win[6] reads 'Diana'.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is Irelia x6 then Diana, which matches the content layer and matches the prose in phases[0..5].why. The full layer was the stale half.
audit.corrected: phases[0..5].side -> Irelia, phases[6].side -> Diana, with phases[6].rating and phases[6].why rewritten to match the new verdict.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 text claimed Vanguard's Edge knocks up, and the early game claimed Diana 'has no escape and no gap-closer until her ultimate unlocks'.
audit.why: Irelia's R Marks and walls, no displacement. Lunar Rush is a level-1-accessible 825-range dash on 22/20/18/16/14s, and it costs NOTHING when dashing to a Moonlight-afflicted target — she has a gap-closer from level 3 onward, and its real cooldown depends entirely on whether Crescent Strike hit you.
audit.corrected: Knockup removed; Lunar Rush's conditional-free cooldown stated as the lane's actual clock.

audit.whatIsWrong: Pale Cascade's shield was never mentioned, Crescent Strike was called 'long cooldown' (it is 8/7.5/7/6.5/6s), and wants.you[1] called Moonlight her passive.
audit.why: Her passive is Moonsilver Blade; Moonlight is the Q debuff that makes Lunar Rush free. Pale Cascade shields every 15/13.5/12/10.5/9s and gains extra strength if the third sphere detonates — it eats the burst window Irelia's four-stack all-in depends on. Irelia's E also grounds, which denies Lunar Rush.
audit.corrected: Shield-first sequencing written into carry, feeding, tradeGood and the do's; grounding-vs-Lunar-Rush stated.

audit.why: The decisive numbers are Lunar Rush 22s->14s (free while Moonlight is up), Crescent Strike 8s->6s, Pale Cascade 15s->9s, Moonfall 100/90/80s at 475 range.

audit.whatIsWrong: Twelve misgendered fields calling Diana he/his, plus dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d pasted from tradeGood/tradeBad.
audit.why: Lint MISGENDER and COPY_PASTE_BLEED; diana is she/her.
audit.corrected: Fixed in every non-report field plus report[0] and report[1]; the rest noted.

edits.before: - Diana Crescent Strike: matchup-defining — Moonlight marks reset her dash — sidestep the arc and her dive has no follow-up. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your W Defiant Dance like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.

edits.before: Diana wins by landing Crescent Strike, denying your pattern, and starting the fight your kit wanted ten seconds later.
edits.after: Diana wins by landing Crescent Strike, riding the free Lunar Rush onto you, and shielding through the trade with Pale Cascade.

edits.before: If Diana takes first blood, tighten up: Crescent Strike is now always up in your head. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn’t — farm with Q resets and stay relevant through stacked windows.
edits.after: If Diana takes first blood, stop standing in Crescent Strike's arc — Moonlight makes her Lunar Rush free and the dive follows it. Farm what Bladesurge can reach, and step up only once Pale Cascade's shield is already spent.

edits.before: Carry through the dance — the wave funds dives no cooldown can, and your R turns skirmishes into no-exit interviews.
edits.after: Carry by eating the shield first: pop Pale Cascade on the wave, then four stacks and an E-stun leave her no free Lunar Rush.

edits.before: You are the front-to-back blender: Q through their line, stun the carries, and let the marks ground the peel.
edits.after: You are the front-to-back blender: Q through their line, E-stun the carries, and let R's wall slow whoever peels.

edits.before: Ahead, dance louder: crash waves into Diana's face, stun the answers, and surf resets through every river fight.
edits.after: Ahead, deny her the arc: hug the wave so Crescent Strike hits minions, and her dash costs a full 22s every time.

edits.before: Best wave: a slow push of low-HP minions — every one is a dash and the crash is an all-in announcement you control. Worst wave: a crashed wave and an empty lane — no minions, no dashes, no Irelia. Crash timing: every crash should buy something — a reset, a plate, a roam. Autopilot shoving buys ganks.
edits.after: Best wave: a slow push of low-HP minions between you and her — each is a Bladesurge and the crash is an all-in you control. Worst wave: a crashed wave and an empty lane, where Crescent Strike lands free and there is nothing left for you to dash to. Crash timing: crash once her shield is spent — buy a plate, a reset, or a roam with it.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 continue the pattern since she still lacks a gap-closer to answer your engage
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay yours: Lunar Rush is a 22s cooldown unless Crescent Strike marked you first

edits.before: Diana's Crescent Strike has a tall skillshot and long cooldown pre-6, so a level 3 dash-in the moment she misses it punishes her hard before her all-in tools exist.
edits.after: Crescent Strike is only an 8s cooldown, but a miss means Lunar Rush costs her the full 22s, so a level 3 dash-in the instant the arc whiffs finds her with no dash to answer.

edits.before: Moonfall pulls you to her, but Vanguard's Edge knocks up first if you initiate — whoever lands their engage first usually wins this all-in, so contest it aggressively.
edits.after: Moonfall pulls you in at 475 range, but Vanguard's Edge Marks her at 950 and refunds Bladesurge — whoever engages first wins this all-in, so contest it aggressively.

edits.before: Diana's early kit revolves entirely around landing Crescent Strike, and if she whiffs it she has almost no follow-up before level 6 — that miss window is your cue to dash in and punish hard. Her passive Moonlight only procs off spell hits, so denying free pokes early keeps her damage output low through the laning phase. Push the wave and force trades on your terms; she has no escape and no gap-closer until her ultimate unlocks.
edits.after: Diana's early kit revolves entirely around landing Crescent Strike, and a miss means Lunar Rush costs her the full 22s instead of nothing — that whiff window is your cue to dash in and punish hard. Moonlight only lands off her spell hits, so denying free arcs cuts her damage and her mobility at once. Push the wave and force trades on your terms; make her spend Pale Cascade's shield on minions before you ever commit.

edits.before: Level 6 is close but still yours if you play it right — Moonfall pulls her to you, which sounds like her win condition, but Vanguard's Edge lets you initiate first with a knockup that beats her to the punch. Whoever commits first usually wins this all-in, so don't sit back and wait for her to pull; force the engage yourself the moment she's in range. Roams are roughly even since neither of you has hard disengage, so play off wave state.
edits.after: Level 6 is close but still yours if you play it right — Moonfall only reaches 475, while Vanguard's Edge reaches 950, Marks her and refunds Bladesurge, so you arrive before the pull does. Whoever commits first usually wins this all-in, so don't wait for her to pull; force the engage the moment she is in range with her shield already down. Roams lean your way since your E-stun converts a gank on its own.

edits.before: Deny her stacking Moonlight passive by trading before she gets free procs
edits.after: Deny Moonlight by hugging the wave so Crescent Strike hits minions

edits.before: Wait for Moonfall to come online before committing to any all-in
edits.after: Mark you with Crescent Strike first so Lunar Rush costs her nothing
